note_on_method: Two of the five filter slugs have a lawful data driver in Mount Pleasant. Free does, because the Town writes "Drop-in play is free" under three of its four venues and prices the fourth. Indoor does, because the Town's own page is split under the headings Indoor and Outdoor and three venues sit under the first. Outdoor has two venues - Miriam Brown and the Park West tennis courts - and lights has one, so neither reaches the three a page needs. Public has none anywhere on this site, because access_type has no controlled vocabulary yet.

slots.why_this_filter: Three of Mount Pleasant's four venues are free, and the Town says so under each one rather than leaving it to be assumed. Park West Gym: "Drop-in play is free." The Deb Gym at Town Hall: the same sentence. Miriam Brown Community Center: "Drop-in play is free and first come, first served." Park West Tennis Courts: "Drop-in play is first come first served and free." Eighteen of the town's nineteen courts are on this page - ten at Park West, four at the Deb Gym, four at Miriam Brown - and they carry every scheduled session in Mount Pleasant except the Senior Center's afternoons. This directory records a price only when an operator publishes one, which is why a free page is not something every city has: a parks department that does not charge for a court rarely thinks to write down that it is free. Mount Pleasant wrote it down four times. It is one of seven cities on this site with a verified free court. Free here comes with conditions the Town states in the same paragraph, and they belong on this page as much as the price does. In the gyms you must sign in, and you play at the session times and not otherwise. Outdoors the net is free on weekdays, from the Program Building at Park West or the G.M. Darby Building at Miriam Brown, and your own responsibility after 5:00 p.m. and at weekends. Paddles and balls are never provided at a free venue. And the Town's coached clinics and private lessons, at Miriam Brown and the Deb Gym, carry resident and non-resident prices of their own, which are lesson prices; nothing on this page charges for the court.
slots.what_qualifies: A venue appears here when the Town of Mount Pleasant states that drop-in play on it costs nothing. Three qualify. Park West qualifies twice over, because the Town prices both of its entries at the same address - the gym under Indoor and the tennis courts under Outdoor - with the word free. The Deb Gym at Town Hall qualifies on "Drop-in play is free." Miriam Brown Community Center qualifies on "Drop-in play is free and first come, first served." The Senior Center is excluded, and deliberately. Its court is "free for members of the Senior Center" and a guest fee for everyone else, "$5 for Mt. Pleasant residents and $10 for those residing outside of Mt. Pleasant", and play is for people 50 and older. Free for a member is not free for the public, so it publishes with a drop-in fee of $5 and the non-resident rate in its notes, and it stays off this page. That is a closer call than it looks: it is the one Mount Pleasant venue that provides the paddles and balls as well as the net, so for a member it is the cheapest court in town. What also does not qualify is anything the Town prices as instruction. Clinics at $50 for residents and $80 for non-residents, private lessons by the hour, packages of four and six: all of it sits on the same page as the free courts and none of it is a court fee. Nothing was refused in Mount Pleasant, so nothing is absent from this page for want of an address or a count.

faqs.a: Yes, in the Town's words under each entry: "Drop-in play is free." This site describes a venue as free only when the operator writes it, and Mount Pleasant does, for three venues and both halves of Park West.

faqs.q: Why is the Senior Center not on this page?
faqs.a: Because it is free for members only. Non-members pay a guest fee of $5 as Mount Pleasant residents or $10 otherwise, and play is for people 50 and older. It publishes with a drop-in fee.

faqs.q: Do I need to sign in?
faqs.a: In the gyms, yes: "All players MUST sign in" at Park West Gym and the Deb Gym. Outdoors the Town states no sign-in.
In the gyms it is provided. Outdoors it is lent on weekdays, from the Program Building at Park West or the G.M. Darby Building at Miriam Brown; outside those hours bring your own.
No. Clinics are $50 for residents and $80 for non-residents, and private lessons are priced by the hour. Those are lesson prices; the courts themselves cost nothing.

slots.why_this_filter: Eleven of Mount Pleasant's nineteen verified courts are indoors, at three of its four venues, and the Town states it in the plainest way an operator can: its pickleball page is divided under two headings, Indoor and Outdoor, and the Senior Center, Park West Gym and The Deb Gym at Town Hall sit under the first. This site publishes an indoor-or-outdoor answer only when an operator states one, and Mount Pleasant states it for every court. Indoor here means a gymnasium floor at a scheduled time. The Town's schedule link calls it "Open Play Schedule in Gyms (including Basketball & Badminton)", nets are "provided for players to set up", and players are told to "enter at their designated time and prepare for breakdown a few minutes prior to end time". So an indoor court in Mount Pleasant exists for its session and not otherwise: Tuesday and Thursday mornings and listed autumn Sundays at Park West Gym, Monday afternoon and Wednesday and Friday mornings at the Deb Gym, three weekday afternoons at the Senior Center for players 50 and older. Between them the three gyms cover every weekday and, in the autumn of 2026, eight Sundays; none of them has an evening. The Deb Gym's four courts become two from September 18 to October 31 for volleyball season, and Park West Gym is closed for voting on November 3. The reason to want this page is a court that does not depend on daylight or weather, and Mount Pleasant has more of them than it has outdoor courts. Two of the three are free; the third is free for members of the Senior Center and a $5 or $10 guest fee otherwise. Bring paddles and balls to the two gyms; the Senior Center provides them.
slots.what_qualifies: A venue appears here when the Town of Mount Pleasant lists it under the Indoor heading of its pickleball page with a count, and this site records that count as indoor courts. Three qualify. Park West, on "Park West Gym / 6 Courts", the largest indoor count in the town and one the Town states a second time in its tournament notice as "6 Indoor Courts"; the venue also holds four outdoor courts, which are added to make its ten and do not appear on this page. The Deb Gym at Town Hall, on "The Deb Gym at Town Hall / 4 Courts", qualifying on four through volleyball season because the count is stated and the reduction to two is printed beside it. The Senior Center, on "Mount Pleasant Senior Center 50+ / 1 Court", which qualifies on one court and carries its own conditions: players 50 and older, free for members, a guest fee for everyone else. A count and a heading are what put a venue here; a fee and an age condition do not take it off. What does not qualify is any court the Town lists under Outdoor. Miriam Brown Community Center's four and the Park West tennis courts' four are outdoor in the Town's own arrangement of the page, and the Park West four are the town's only lit courts, so evening play in Mount Pleasant is an outdoor matter. No gymnasium is counted because it is a gymnasium: each of these three counts is the Town's own line, not an inference from the presence of a basketball court.

faqs.q: When can I play indoors in Mount Pleasant?
faqs.a: Park West Gym Tuesdays and Thursdays 8:00 am to noon and listed Sundays; the Deb Gym Mondays 1:00 to 3:00 pm, Wednesdays 9:00 am to noon and Fridays 8:00 am to noon; the Senior Center Tuesday and Thursday 3:00 to 4:50 pm and Friday 3:00 to 5:50 pm.
Park West Gym and the Deb Gym are, in the Town's words. The Senior Center is free for members and a $5 or $10 guest fee for non-members, for players 50 and older.

faqs.q: Is there an evening indoor session?
faqs.a: No. Every indoor session the Town prints is a weekday morning or afternoon, or an autumn Sunday morning at Park West Gym. The evening group plays outdoors on the lit Park West tennis courts.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net?
faqs.a: No; nets are provided at all three. Bring paddles and balls to the two gyms. The Senior Center provides those as well.

faqs.q: Why are there sometimes only two courts at the Deb Gym?
faqs.a: Volleyball season. From September 18 to October 31 the Town says open gym "will only be played on two pickleball courts"; in the other weeks it is four.
